value.rationale: The four-cube is a canonical 16-vertex, four-colour Cartesian power, and this determines the exact minimum number of edges that must be made universally available for all four monochromatic connectivity requirements. The construction attains the known ceiling bound in the first nontrivial four-colour cube and advances the next 32-vertex product case to a one-edge interval. The precise finite values offer substantive benchmarks for the newly studied Cartesian-product wild-number question, without pretending to solve all dimensions.
